stages.line: You are still numb from losing {lost}. You go through the motions and say little.
You have started to talk about {lost} now, in small bits, when you feel safe.
stages.journal: {name} has begun to speak of the loss.

stages.line: The grief for {lost} has settled into something you can carry. You laugh sometimes again.
You are saving every coin you can toward expanding your {job_place}.
You have drawn up plans to expand your {job_place} and talk about them to anyone who will listen.
stages.journal: {name} has plans to grow the business.

stages.line: You have started building. It has cost more than you expected, but it is yours.
You never speak of it, but you keep a tally of coins hidden away against the day you can buy your freedom.
The hidden tally has grown. You let yourself imagine what you would do with a free day.
There is a quarrel in your family that no one will mention, and it weighs on you.
You have decided to reach out first, though you do not know how.
The quarrel has been mended, awkwardly, and the house is lighter for it.
You feel you have something to prove, and few chances to prove it.
You are waiting for a real chance, and are quicker to volunteer than you used to be.
